newsitem.title: TANZANIA: Tanzania to host meetings on Burundi crisis.
newsitem.headline: Tanzania to host meetings on Burundi crisis.

text.p: Tanzania plans to host a series of meetings in the coming week including a regional summit on the crisis in Burundi, officials and diplomats said on Wednesday.

An official said Tanzanian President Benjamin Mkapa left for Lusaka on Wednesday to press for regional heads of state to attend a summit on Burundi on April 16 in the northern Tanzanian town of Arusha.

Diplomats told Reuters Mkapa would probably use a meeting of the Common Market of Eastern and Southern Africa (COMESA) to lobby for approval for Burundi military ruler Pierre Buyoya to attend the talks next Wednesday.
They said Mkapa was likely to raise the issue of regional economic sanctions against Burundi, imposed shortly after Buyoya seized power in a coup by the Tutsi-dominated army last July.
The main aim of the sanctions was to force Buyoya into peace talks with the rebels.

Diplomats said if approval was obtained for Buyoya to attend next Wednesday's meeting he would be invited as a "faction head" and not as head of state. He has not attended previous summits on Burundi.
They said former Tanzanian president Julius Nyerere, the international mediator on Burundi, was organising a meeting in Dar es Salaam to which Burundian rebel chief Leonard Nyangoma would be invited.
Nyerere will also chair talks between Burundi's factions on Friday and Saturday in Arusha as part of his long campaign to hammer out an agreement between them on ending the civil war.
More than 150,000 people have been killed in massacres and civil war between the Tutsi-dominated army and Hutu rebels since the killing of Burundi's first freely-elected president in 1993.
